subject: Post-demo recommended model trio + perf/cost tradeoffs and next steps
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@clearline.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.inference>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@clearline.health>
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from demo — model candidates & benchmarks

Evelyn / team —

Thanks for the demo this morning. Elena and I ran through the transcript and have a couple quick asks so we can prioritize internally: 

- Can you send the list of recommended models (3–4) you think fit our triage use case, with a short rationale for each?
- We need p95 latency and approximate $/1k-token cost estimates for our expected request profile (avg input ~120 tokens, avg output ~220).
- Any prompt sets, known quality regressions, or hallucination sensitivity notes would be super helpful.

High-level constraints from our side: PHI redaction pre-send (will run in our VPC), p95 target <= 350ms for short prompts, and monthly spend target ~ $12k for pilot.

Can you get this by EOD tomorrow? If not, a quick prioritized shortlist and pointers to the benchmarks is fine.

- Samir

---

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearline.health>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@clearline.health>
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — model candidates & benchmarks

Samir / Elena —

Appreciate the clarity on constraints. Attached are the artifacts and a compact recommendation to help you move quickly. Attached: CLH-benchmark-summary-20271003.pdf, prompt_set_v1.csv, benchmark-run-42.txt. Below is a concise shortlist with tradeoffs tailored to your latency/cost targets.

Recommended trio (fast reference):

1) Redwood-Edge-7B-quant (candidate A) — Best latency / cost
   - Rationale: Quantized 7B variant tuned for prefix caching. Excellent at short-turn interactions and low inference cost.
   - Performance: p95 latency ~ 180–260ms on dedicated 1xA100-equivalent with our batching profile for your avg 120/220 token shape.
   - Cost: Estimated $2.8 / 1k output tokens (pilot config, includes caching).
   - Quality notes: Very good for instruction-following; occasional brevity and mild paraphrase artifacts on long context. Lower hallucination on extraction prompts.

2) Redwood-Atlas-13B-mix (candidate B) — Balanced quality / cost
   - Rationale: 13B mixed-precision variant; stronger on complex synth/summarization tasks with modest latency hit.
   - Performance: p95 latency ~ 320–420ms (can be tightened with dedicated endpoint and tuned batching).
   - Cost: Estimated $5.4 / 1k output tokens.
   - Quality notes: Better factuality and coherence for multi-step reasoning. Slightly more token generation overhead.

3) Falcon-40B-Instruct (candidate C) — Highest raw quality / fallback for hard cases
   - Rationale: Top-tier for difficult QA and edge-case generation, but higher cost and latency. Good as a canary fallback for flagged queries.
   - Performance: p95 latency ~ 700ms+ unless pinned to heavy capacity.
   - Cost: Estimated $14+ / 1k output tokens. Use selectively for escalation.

Quick notes on safety/PHI handling and regressions:
- We reviewed prompt_set_v1.csv against a small PHI-synthetic set. Candidate B had the fewest hallucination failures on the summary tests; A was fine when prefix redaction was applied.
- Benchmark run details: https://bench.redwood.inference/run/42 (summary attached as benchmark-run-42.txt). The attached PDF includes token-distribution charts and the cost model assumptions.

Suggested pilot configuration to hit your p95 <= 350ms target and $12k/mo budget: primary endpoint on candidate A (Redwood-Edge-7B-quant) with candidate B (Atlas-13B) as a warm fallback for queries that exceed a quality threshold. Start with conservative batching and prefix caching enabled.

Next steps I suggest:
- Confirm whether you want candidate B as live fallback or only for offline scoring.
- If live fallback, we can schedule a 30-min ops call this week to size the Dedicated pool and finalize PO.
- I can share a short canary playbook (rollout steps + metrics) and a prompt hardening checklist.

Attaching the prompt set and the benchmark summary per your request. Happy to iterate on the cost model if you share monthly token profile.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Elena Morales <elena@clearline.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.inference>, Samir Patel <samir@clearline.health>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — model candidates & benchmarks

Evelyn — thanks, this is really helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we sync with procurement: 

- For candidate A, is the p95 number above measured with prefix caching enabled? If we perform PHI redaction on our side (pre-send) will that materially change the latency profile?
- For candidate B as live fallback, what does the rollback path look like if we see a quality regression during the pilot?
- Can you confirm whether your Dedicated offering can be scoped to our Azure tenancy (we require data-in-region for initial pilot)?

Also, Samir flagged the $12k/mo target — the $2.8 /1k number for candidate A looks fine but we want a quick sensitivity calc if average output tokens creep to 350 tokens. Can you provide that in the follow-up?

Thanks — Elena

On Sun, Oct 3, 2027 at 4:05 PM Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.inference> wrote:
> (attached)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearline.health>, Elena Morales <elena@clearline.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — model candidates & benchmarks

Elena / Samir —

Answers inline and concrete next steps below. Adding Marissa (Sales) and Karthik (Solutions/Infra) to scope procurement and the canary plan.

1) Latency and PHI redaction impact
- The p95 number for candidate A (180–260ms) in the attached runs assumes prefix caching enabled and a modest batching window (15ms). If you do pre-send PHI redaction on your side, latency impact is negligible on our path (redaction happens before the network hop). The bigger latency delta comes from network egress to the Dedicated pool in-region — Karthik will confirm AZ sizing but our Azure-region deployments match the numbers within ±20% on p95 depending on instance type.

2) Rollback path for candidate B fallback
- Canary approach we recommend: 5% traffic to candidate B for 72 hours with side-by-side quality metrics (we provide automatic trace comparison and a quick scoring hook). If quality drifts (>3% regression on your eval rubric or user-reported escalations >2%), automatic fallback to candidate A is triggered and we open a hotfix ticket. Rollback is immediate (route switch) and we maintain cold-start mitigations.

3) Dedicated in-region support
- Yes — Dedicated can be scoped to Azure tenancy. Karthik: will follow up with a sizing note and a short document describing VNet peering and KMS options.

4) Cost sensitivity for candidate A at 350 avg out tokens
- Base estimate we provided: $2.8 /1k output tokens at avg 220 output tokens. At 350 tokens the unit cost scales roughly 1.59x → est $4.5 /1k output tokens. With prefix caching and request-level caching we often keep effective cost lower on repeat calls. I attached a small sensitivity table in the PDF.

Proposed immediate next steps (action items):
- CLH: confirm whether you'd like candidate B as a live fallback or offline scorer (reply to this thread).
- CLH: confirm pilot start window (target week of 10/18) so we can reserve Dedicated capacity.
- Redwood: provide canary playbook + 30-min ops call (Karthik to propose times).
- Procurement: Marissa can start a PO template and share initial T&C; Marissa, can you loop in Finance?

If that plan sounds ok I'll send a short one-page canary playbook and a proposed PO estimate for a 4-week pilot (~expected token volume, uplift buffers, and rollback guardrails).

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to pilot.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: CLH-benchmark-summary-20271003.pdf; prompt_set_v1.csv; benchmark-run-42.txt
